tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.

IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

## 7. Questions for arbitration

Each question gives the passage, the readings, and a program whose verdict changes, with its witness. The policy readings (`R/policy.md`) and every entry of `R/readings/*.md` are also submitted (Q23).

**Q1. §63 versus §49.8 and §57 (B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B8, B10).**
- Passages: §57, "On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees: WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan". §49 item 8, "every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place". §58, "An `ok` transition must … preserve the relevant invariants". §63 lists preconditions 1–8, and none requires the destination to remain usable.
- Readings:
  - (a) §63 as written, so §57 is false (current model);
  - (b) add to §63 "destination usable in the resulting state" (the draft clause), which makes `reachableDU_kinv` the unconditional §57 (`R/reports/kernel-main.md` P-M1);
  - (c) another repair chosen by the spec owner.
- Program: statics `src` (leaf 0, `Init`) and `prov` (leaf 1, `Init`); `alloc(prov, owner 0)` makes place 2; `alloc(prov, owner 2)` makes place 3; then `transfer(0, 3)`. Under (a) the transfer is `ok`, places 2 and 3 own each other and §49.8 fails. Under (b) it is `reject`.
- Witnesses: `Access.transfer_breaks_kinv` (Transfer.lean:781), `Access.reachable_kinv_false` (Main.lean:685), `Access.transfer_kinv_iff` (Main.lean:465).

**Q2. §76.6 (B33).**
- Passage: "Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld`, and the expected arena invariants."
- Readings:
  - (G) the whole kernel state and every live entry (`Arena.NewArena766Global`, Arena.lean:2273);
  - (L) only the relations of the new arena (`Arena.NewArena766Local`, :2319);
  - a mixed reading (kernel predicates over the whole state, ArenaInv of the new entry only);
  - in each case, evaluated on the departure or the arrival state. The arrival choice changes no verdict (`newArena766Global_arrival_iff`).
- Programs:
  - Run U (`Arena.Witness.newArena766_global_fails_local_holds`, :2649): the model accepts, (G) and the mixed reading reject, (L) accepts.
  - Run V (`Arena.Witness.newArena766_local_fails`, :2703): the model accepts, and every reading rejects.
- Also to settle: whether `NewArenaBase` (:153) should then carry the chosen reading.

**Q3. §36 ¶2 last sentence and §89 s4 vs HandlePool D.3 (B35).**
- Passages: §36, "These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel". §89, "These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel". D.3, "aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres" and "L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`".
- Readings:
  - (reachability) every kernel state of a library run is in `Reachable`;
  - (step-level) the kernel effect of each library step is that of a `KSeq` of accepted kernel steps from the same state.
- Program: `freeSlot(⟨0, 0, 0⟩)` on `v3`, which the contract accepts. Kernel `endUse` is rejected at slot place 1 and at storage root 0, and the arrival state `k5` is reached by O1–O16 alone (`Lib.HandlePool.Witness.freeSlot_lands_in_reachable`, HandlePool.lean:2183).
  - Under the reachability reading this run conforms (proved).

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer

**Preconditions**

1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved.
5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.

**`ok` effect:**

- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.

A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.

## 64. O5 — Explicit Attachment of an Anchor

**Preconditions**

1. `result` is a usable place over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.

## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset

Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance does not permit reading a former logical value without the required initialization.

## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value

A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.

## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles

An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.

## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

## 90. Global and Called Frame

Global storage is anchored to the base frame, but a called function does not acquire ambient authority to modify it merely by being invoked. To access a global, it receives a derived authority under `enterFrame` conditions and may exercise only its effective modes.

the right to create ... exclusive authority over the administered storage". `AllocStatic.providerRight`

import Ern.Lib.HandlePool
open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.Lib.HandlePool Ern.Lib.HandlePool.Witness Examples

namespace P1Alt
/-- resolve(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩, Modify) on w4: companion 4 from internal 3, entry 5 over slot place 1. -/
def u5 : PState := { w4 with
  kern := deriveEff (compS w4.kern pl4 .modify) w4.kern.A.length (footprint w4.kern.P 1) .modify
  res := w4.res ++ [⟨pl4.id, pl4.internal, w4.kern.A.length, .modify,
    [(w4.kern.A.length + 1, 0, 0)]⟩] }
/-- client write of slot place 1 through the ENTRY authority 5 (not internal). -/
def u6 : PState := { u5 with kern := write3Eff u5.kern [1] }
/-- unresolve(4): release entry 5, then companion 4. -/
def u7 : PState := { u6 with kern := releaseEff (releaseEff u6.kern 5) 4 }

#eval (List.range 6).map fun j => (j, u6.kern.afp j, u6.kern.org j, decide (u6.kern.Active j))
#eval findRes u6 4 |>.map fun r => (r.comp, r.entries, unresolveList u6.kern r)

theorem u7_reach : PReachI K0 hst u7 := by
  have r5 : ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify w4 (.ok u5) :=
    .ok (pl := pl4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  have h5 : PReachI K0 hst u5 := .step w4_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.resolve r5)
  have h6 : PReachI K0 hst u6 := .step h5 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.write (a := 5) (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
  have hl : unresolveList u6.kern ⟨0, 3, 4, .modify, [(5, 0, 0)]⟩ = [5, 4] := by decide
  have hp5 : ReleasePre u6.kern 5 := by decide
  have hp4 : ReleasePre (releaseEff u6.kern 5) 4 := by decide
  have hra : releaseAll u6.kern (unresolveList u6.kern ⟨0, 3, 4, .modify, [(5, 0, 0)]⟩) =
      some (releaseEff (releaseEff u6.kern 5) 4) := by
    rw [hl]; simp only [releaseAll, hp5, hp4, ↓reduceIte]
  exact .step h6 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.unresolve (c := 4) (.ok (r := ⟨0, 3, 4, .modify, [(5, 0, 0)]⟩) (by decide) hra))

/-- Same facts as `freeSlot_lands_in_reachable`'s step-level part, on a run whose only client
kernel step is a write through an entry authority (no client use of `internal` or a companion). -/
theorem alt :
    PReachI K0 hst u7 ∧ u7.kern.I 1 = .init ∧ ¬ EndUsePre K0 u7.kern 1 ∧
    ¬ EndUsePre K0 u7.kern 0 ∧ ∃ L', FreeSlotStep K0 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ u7 (.ok L') := by
  have hok : FreeSlotStep K0 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ u7 (.ok _) :=
    .ok (pl := pl4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  exact ⟨u7_reach, by decide, by decide, by decide, _, hok⟩

#print axioms alt
end P1Alt

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. No verdict changes on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft].

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack (`Stack.block` gives none): DS-v1 says nothing. Reading [draft
`case_grow`]: `reject` (`GrowStep.noBlock`). Alternative: `fail`, by analogy with DS-v1 "rewind m
fails on a dead or foreign mark" (an identifier the stack does not record). Example
(`Ern.Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`, decided): after
`grow(0, 6, 1)` replaced block 6 by block 9 (`ds03.stacks` records the blocks `[⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩]`
only), `grow(0, 6, 1)` is `reject` here and `fail` under the alternative (the step reaches
`noBlock` and no other rule).

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example

/-! ## Preservation by every step except `transfer` (§57, §58) -/

/-- Every operation other than `transfer` preserves `KInv` (§57) from its `ok` outcome, under
`DDSound` (§80, used by `split`, §61). -/
theorem op_preserves {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k) (hinv : KInv s)
    (h : op.Step k s (.ok s')) (hnt : ∀ src dst, op ≠ .transfer src dst) : KInv s' := by
  cases op with
  | derive => exact derive_preserves hinv h
  | split => exact split_preserves hdd hinv h
  | release => exact release_preserves hinv h
  | transfer src dst => exact absurd rfl (hnt src dst)
  | depend => exact depend_preserves hinv h
  | enter => exact enter_preserves hinv h
  | exit => exact exit_preserves hinv h
  | read => exact read_preserves hinv h
  | write => exact write_preserves hinv h
  | writeShared => exact writeShared_preserves hinv h
  | pin => exact pin_preserves hinv h
  | unpin => exact unpin_preserves hinv h
  | endUse => exact endUse_preserves hinv h
  · obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, rfl⟩ := Frames.exit_get hy
    have hs := Frames.exitG_active ya
    unfold Survives at hs; rw [hy₀] at hs
    have hl : HolderLive ({ s with F := s.F.tail } : S3) y₀.holder := hs.2
    rw [(Frames.exitG_same s s.F.tail j y₀).2.2]
    refine ⟨(hlive _).2 hl, fun e => ?_⟩
    rw [e, htop] at hl; exact hnot hl

/-- A kernel step whose `transfer`, if it is one, leaves its destination usable (§63). The
condition is a hypothesis on runs, not a clause of §63 nor of §57. -/
def KStepDU (k : K) (s s' : S3) : Prop :=
  ∃ op : KernelOp, op.Step k s (.ok s') ∧ ∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst

/-- States reached from `S3.init statics` by runs whose transfers keep the destination usable
(§57, restricted by the hypothesis of `KStepDU`, which is not a clause of §63). -/
inductive ReachableDU (k : K) (statics : Statics) : S3 → Prop where
  /-- The initial state (§47). -/
  | init : ReachableDU k statics (S3.init statics)
  /-- One more step of `KStepDU` (§57). -/
  | step {s s' : S3} : ReachableDU k statics s → KStepDU k s s' → ReachableDU k statics s'

/-- From a state satisfying `KInv` (§57) and `HeldAnchored` (auxiliary) under `DDSound` (§80),
the steps of `KStepDU` are exactly the kernel steps whose resulting state satisfies `KInv`: the
restriction of `ReachableDU` keeps exactly the runs along which §57 holds. -/
theorem kstepDU_iff {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k) (hinv : KInv s)
    (hheld : HeldAnchored s) : KStepDU k s s' ↔ KStep k s s' ∧ KInv s' := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨op, hop, hdu⟩
    exact ⟨kstep_iff.2 ⟨op, hop⟩, (op_preserves_of_dst_usable hdd hinv hheld hop hdu).1⟩
  · rintro ⟨h, hk⟩
    obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 h
    refine ⟨op, hop, fun src dst e => ?_⟩
    subst e
    exact transfer_dst_usable_of_noDangling hinv.1 hop hk.2.1.2.2

/-- A state of `ReachableDU` is reachable (§57). -/
theorem ReachableDU.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3}
    (h : ReachableDU k statics s) : Reachable k statics s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨op, hop, -⟩ := h
    exact .step ih (kstep_iff.2 ⟨op, hop⟩)

structure TransferPre (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §63.1: `source` is usable. -/
  srcUsable : s.Usable src
  /-- §63.1: `destination` is usable. -/
  dstUsable : s.Usable dst
  /-- §63.1: exercisable `Modify` over the source. -/
  srcRight : HasRight s .modify src
  /-- §63.1: exercisable `Modify` over the destination. -/
  dstRight : HasRight s .modify dst
  /-- §63.2: same shape of ordered subtrees. -/
  sameShape : SameShape s.P src dst
  /-- §63.3: all source leaves are `Init`. -/
  srcInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init
  /-- §63.3: no destination leaf is `Init`. -/
  dstNotInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init
  /-- §63.3: source and destination footprints are disjoint. -/
  disjoint : ¬ overlap s.P src dst
  /-- §63.4: no active derived authority covers a source leaf from outside the source. -/
  noOutsideDerived : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j
  /-- §63.5: no in-place source leaf is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false
  /-- §63.6: dependencies of the usable places following the value are valid. -/
  depsValid : ∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src, s.Active x
  /-- §63.6: `AnchorOrder` in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrder : AnchorOrder (transferEff s src dst)
  /-- §63.7: every moved held authority satisfies `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : ∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length, AnchorMoves s src x →
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
      OptP ((transferEff s src dst).A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
        EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)) True
  /-- §63.8: local self-blocking prevention. -/
  noSelfLock : NoLocalSelfLock s src dst

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `transfer` (§63). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :

/-- Preconditions of `store` (§65). -/
structure StorePre (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §65.1: the authority is active, derived, and held by the current frame. -/
  derivedHeld : OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧
    y.holder = .frame s.top) False
  /-- §65.2: `target` is usable. -/
  usable : s.Usable p
  /-- §65.2: `target` is a leaf. -/
  leaf : isLeaf s.P p
  /-- §65.2: exercisable `Modify` over `target`. -/
  right : HasRight s .modify p
  /-- §65.2: `target` holds no active authority. -/
  free : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
    OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place p) True
  /-- §65.3: the authority covers no leaf of `target` nor of storage it owns, transitively. -/
  noCover : ∀ l ∈ s.afp a, l ∉ footprint s.P p ∧
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, OwnedIn s.P p q → l ∉ footprint s.P q
  /-- §65.4: the effective anchor respects `AnchorOrder` relative to the frame of `target`. -/
  anchorOrder : EffAnchorOK s a (s.pframe p)
  /-- §65.5: in the resulting state, `target` is under exercisable `Modify`. -/
  keepsTarget : HasRight (storeEff s a p) .modify p
  /-- §65.5: `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeld (storeEff s a p)
